title: Bonus Chapter: The Spear Hero's Sneak Peek 2
text: Sleeping Cat and Waking Bird

That was a memory from a certain day, I say. It was an unremarkable day when Father, back when he was still the first Shield Hero, was tending to the monster stables in the village as part of his usual morning routine. I too was over in the Filolial stables next door, enjoying a refreshing morning.
“Ku… Kue.”
“Kue.”
The Filolial-samas suddenly grew restless, glancing all around, before all turning to face the same direction in unison. I was wondering just what had happened when—
“Naofumi-sama!”

Father had just stepped out of the monster stables when Big Sister’s voice rang out with unusual intensity, so I found myself heading outside as well, over toward where Father and the others were. The whole village was already up and about, looking forward to breakfast, and they too tilted their heads curiously at the sound of Big Sister’s voice as they watched the scene unfold.
“Ah… looks like we’ve got visitors,” Father muttered, sighing slightly, and set off walking beside Big Sister with a tired air about him.

“Ohh? Seems like something’s come up,” said Older Sister, who had apparently just gotten up despite drinking late into the night. She wasn’t even the least bit drunk, which put everyone nearby on edge.
“Is there some kind of problem, I wonder? Shall Motoyasu handle it, I say?”
“Motoyasu, you don’t need to do anything. There’s no real problem, so just behave yourself.”
“Understood, indeed!”

Father seemed to understand something about the situation. Looking for all the world like he was just heading out for a morning stroll, he walked ahead… toward the village entrance. Thud thud thud thud! The Filolial-samas all lined up together near the entrance, and Rival, for whatever reason, was flat on the ground on the other side, prostrating itself. And there, beyond them… stood a rounded, cat-like Demi-Human standing about a hundred and thirty centimeters tall, alongside a bird-type monster with dazzling plumage evoking crimson flames, its long peacock-like tail feathers trailing behind it. Looking more closely at the cat-like Demi-Human, it had a lizard-like tail covered in fur and was wearing overalls. Some traveler passing through the neighboring town, perhaps? From somewhere around Siltvelt? But judging by the reactions of the Filolial-samas, Rival, and Big Sister, that clearly wasn’t the case. Just what in the world was going on, I wondered?
“Rival, what exactly are you doing, I say?”
“Nano, shut up! Rival doesn’t have time to deal with you right now. Be quiet, nano!”

What a strange reaction. Ah! Look, over there’s a big Filolial-sama! It had the appearance of an ordinary Filolial, but it couldn’t fool these Motoyasu eyes, I say! Just as I was about to approach the large Filolial-sama, Kuu, Marine, and Midori stopped me.
“Mokkun, no!”
“I don’t think you should upset that person’s mood!”
“Goshujin-sama, I feel like you really shouldn’t upset that person’s mood.”
Filo-tan also approached Father, pointing at the bird-type monster beside the cat Demi-Human, warning him too.
“You’re seriously making everyone uncomfortable. Maybe tone it down a little, hm?”
“Nah, nah, I’m not putting off that much of a presence over here, am I? Ahh, this is a problem… I’m supposed to be the casual, laid-back type, you know.”
Somehow it felt exactly like royalty had shown up incognito among commoners—the cat Demi-Human and the bird monster seemed at a loss for how to respond, chatting between themselves.

“Ah, first off, everyone, don’t worry, I don’t have such a difficult personality that I’d get upset over something like this, so feel free to relax. If anything, I’m the one intruding here, just a visitor, that’s all.”
The bird monster spread one wing out like a hand, addressing the Filolial-samas reassuringly. At that, the Filolial-samas seemed to relax slightly, some of the tension draining from them.

“Right, right, ease up, everyone. Sorry for the sudden visit without any warning. We happened to run into an old friend nearby and figured we’d drop by to say hello while introductions were being made. Thought at the very least we ought to greet you properly. Oh, and that bird over there apparently just had something really good happen right before this, so it’s in an especially good mood—won’t get mad no matter what you do right now.”
“As long as your soul isn’t rotten, you can do whatever you like!”

The cat Demi-Human pointed at the bird monster, explaining this to Father. Did something happen if your soul was rotten? According to what Father said, apparently there was no one here with a rotten soul.
“And yet, both the dragon and the Filolials are on high alert regardless.”
“Raph…”
Raph-chan, perched on Father’s shoulder, cried out.
“Ah, that’s because of this troublesome bird here. Being the progenitor of all winged creatures, it’s letting off this bizarre aura without holding back at all. Quite the nuisance, isn’t it?”
“Being popular is a hard cross to bear… though you’re one to talk, letting your own presence leak out everywhere.”
“Mine’s fine because only certain beings can even sense it. Otherwise they wouldn’t notice at all.”
“…If you could hide it, you could’ve just taken that thing down yourself. And what’s with the ‘I was alone’ bit, huh?”
In response to Father, the cat Demi-Human answered with an easy, unbothered expression.

“The other side wasn’t stupid enough to fall for that, you know? Well, maybe they were a little stupid. Anyway, I really was alone back then. I’m not lying, and besides, you wouldn’t leave the fate of the world up to just anyone, would you?”
“Yeah, sure…”
The cat Demi-Human clapped its hands together with a small pop, shifting its gaze away from Father toward the rest of us standing behind him.

“Well then, allow me to properly introduce myself. To you all, I suppose I’d be what’s known as a god-hunter. My name is Ark. I had a bit of an encounter with Naofumi-kun here, and I ended up lending him a hand.”
“Yeah, that’s right.”
“Yes, we were saved by you back then.”

The one who had introduced itself as the cat Demi-Human, now revealed to be the god-hunter Ark, spoke thus. And Father and the others nodded along. So then, this was apparently someone Father owed a great deal to, from back when he was working to defeat the Crimson Swine’s true body. Father turned his gaze toward the bird monster standing beside Ark.

“You’ve probably already heard from Ark, but I’m Naofumi Iwatani. This is Raphtalia beside me. There are plenty of others behind us too, but introducing everyone would take forever, so if you want to talk to them later, go ahead.”
“Sure, sure. My name is… well, like him, I go by a lot of names, but I suppose I’m most often called the Phoenix. Not that I’m immortal or anything, mind you.”
“Well, it wouldn’t make much sense for a bunch of god-hunters to be immortal themselves.”
“Exactly. We just sleep and wake up, that’s all.”
“I mean, that’s not really a name though, is it?”
“I know, I know. There’s also ‘Hōō,’ but that already exists in this world too, doesn’t it? So for simplicity’s sake, just call me Hō—might end up being my next name anyway.”
Having said that, the bird monster who called itself Hō gave a small bow.
“Ah, I also happen to have the role of a god-hunter myself, though it’s different from this one here, who brings eternity to an end.”
At the mention of ending eternity, Hō pointed at Ark. So it had a title like that too, huh.
“Sometimes I’m called the progenitor of all winged creatures too, you know. World renewal is technically his… job, but don’t worry. This world isn’t so old or rotten that it needs renewing.”
It all sounded like quite a grand conversation—were these two on the same level as Ren or Black Thunder, I wondered?
“So you, who seems on par with that one, are you like some kind of dragon progenitor? You’ve got that sort of vibe about you.”
Father asked, looking over at Rival, who still had its head lowered. Meaning—this was Rival’s original source! If that were true, then it was an enemy, I say!
“Hmm? No, compared to the progenitor, Ark thinks it’s more like being siblings, actually. The dragons just sort of treat it as a superior out of formality, but it’s a bit different.”
“Sounds pretty similar to me.”
“Hmm… maybe think of it like an in-law relationship? Does that make more sense?”
No blood relation, but a position like the clan chief’s brother-in-law… I see, that did paint a somewhat different picture, I say.
“Haaah…”
Father let out quite a weary sigh.
“Ah, you don’t need to look so troubled about it. It’d be a shame if you served up a plate of bubuzuke to a visitor from another world, wouldn’t it?”
That was clearly code for “please leave already.” Even looking like that, it knew all about Japanese customs!

“Well… Ark understands the anger, the ‘why now, you’re late, you idiots!’ kind of feeling, but there are countless worlds out there, and it’s not like anyone can help it when certain parties were working to keep the alarms from ever going off. Omniscience and omnipotence are nothing but arrogance anyway—full of holes, through and through.”
Ark let out quite the heartfelt complaint.
“While staying here, at the very least, Ark will let you vent your anger at it. You’ve more than earned that right. Still, would you mind hearing out our side, and a bit of a report?”
“What is it?”
“The mastermind behind this whole affair, in the world where they were operating—they’ve been made to pay. There won’t be any more waves stirred up from that direction.”
Ark stated this flatly. Now that I thought about it, this Ark fellow—I couldn’t sense anything from it at all, not even the faintest presence. Was this what being a god-hunter meant, I wondered?
“…I see.”
Father, having listened to the report calmly, let his frown ease somewhat.

“The person in charge tried making all sorts of excuses, but honestly, it was almost laughable that they thought we wouldn’t dig deeper. The whole world had rotted through, completely, on a systemic level. To them, Ark probably looks like nothing short of a slaughterer.”
Well, whatever the case, Ark laughed… though somehow, that smile felt strangely familiar to me.
“Anyway, that’s why we’ll be staying here a while, if that’s alright.”
“Sure, sure. If you two are around, I bet any troublesome types who show up will just get handled on their own. Just don’t slack off, got it?”
“I know, I know. The least we can do is repay a night’s lodging and a meal.”

Hō ordered the Filolial-samas to disperse, and once they’d settled into relaxing however they pleased, it rejoined the conversation. So, meaning, these two god-hunters would be staying in the village for a while. The villagers too dispersed, whispering among themselves in small chats. What should Motoyasu do now, I wondered? Just as I was thinking of heading back to my daily routine with the Filolial-samas, Hō turned to look at me.
“Ah, you—I recognize you. I remember now. You were making news in a world Hō was staying in before coming here, weren’t you? Motoyasu Kitamura, was it?”
“What? You know about Motoyasu?”

“Told you already, didn’t I? Before coming here, in a world Hō was indebted to, Hō remembered a bit about him. Well, needless to say, he’s quite the celebrity there. Whew-hoo, what a ladies’ man! Just like Hō!”

Father was glaring at me. Or rather, glaring at both me and my spear, to be precise. There was a god-hunter standing right nearby, and you didn’t even notice?! And more to the point, is your world full of nothing but idiots like this?! I could practically feel Father thinking exactly that.
“I—I don’t know anything about that, I say!”
“Well, no surprise you don’t remember. Hō wasn’t quite like this back then… there was a lot going on. Now Hō’s shining this brilliantly, though!”

There seemed to be some kind of story behind it. I didn’t know the details of Hō’s circumstances, but this was a relief, honestly. Still, the vibe was a little cringeworthy, I say. Watching it felt uncomfortably like looking at my past self.
“…The news, huh.”

“Yep. The story was that he’d been killed over some romantic entanglement, but he was actually summoned to this world and managed to avoid death… there are still traces of causal interference from the mastermind behind this whole affair. I see, I see. Since he ‘died,’ all sorts of related parties apparently went on a rampage, and the mastermind met quite a gruesome end because of it. At the university… oh wait, that’s getting into privacy territory Hō shouldn’t be discussing. Sorry about that.”
Hō seemed to be talking about something from my original world. Incredibly, deeply irrelevant information, I say.

“Oh? So he tried to avoid his own destruction by making use of his original nature in an emergency, huh. I see, I see. Purely coincidental, but maybe it was some kind of fate that we and you ended up in the same world together.”
Video Crystal Letter
Ren and Itsuki, responding to my summons, came over to my house, I say.
“Huh? Ren, Itsuki, what are you two doing here?”
Even Father showed up. A bit unexpected, but no matter, I say.
“Yeah, apparently Motoyasu called both of us here separately with a message.”
“I came here wondering just what this could be about.”
“Hmm…”
And so, Ren and Itsuki knocked on the door of my house—knock knock.
“…No answer?”
“Honestly, calling people over and then this.”
“Doesn’t seem to be locked, though?”
“Well then, shall we let ourselves in first? Perhaps it’s something urgent.”
Ren and Itsuki went ahead and stepped inside my house. Inside, there was a video crystal I’d placed on the table, along with a note.
“What is this…?”
“Addressed to us. Looks like it says to play the video crystal.”
“Honestly, what is with that man.”
With a tone of exasperation, Itsuki activated the video crystal. A recording appeared, showing me sitting in a chair with Yuki-chan on my lap.
“Wazzzup! Ren, Itsuki, you watching?”
Ren and Itsuki’s silent, expressionless stares were quite the sight, I say.
“What is this. Sounds like the kind of line someone says right before a cuckolding reveal. So the homewrecker would be Motoyasu-kun, but then who’s the one being cheated on?”
“Based on the visuals, wouldn’t that be Yuki-san?”
“Yuki’s Motoyasu’s Filolial though. Even so, being a homewrecker suits him disturbingly well.”
“Well, Motoyasu-kun is handsome, after all.”
“Waah, what are you doing, let Kitamura-Kou join too!”
“Kuro too!”
Kou and Kuro-chan burst into the recording, mid-filming. The two of them bounced around, tangling themselves up with me while I sat there with Yuki-chan on my lap.
“And just like that, the cuckold video turned into a home video.”
“Seriously, what is going on here?”
“Makes no sense at all.”
“Hold on, we’re in the middle of filming right now, I say. Just be patient a bit.”
“Yaaay, Naofumi-sama, are you watching?”
Yuki-chan called out Father’s name at that point, being considerate toward the Hero who hadn’t been mentioned yet among the group.
“Why is Yuki-chan saying my name at a moment like this? What exactly does that mean?”
“Doesn’t seem like Yuki-san had any deep meaning behind it.”
“Yeah, no doubt she has no idea what it even means.”
Time to start over, I say. Since re-filming would’ve been a hassle, I just kept rolling as is.
“Now then, the reason I called you two here today is no small matter. There is a certain truth I must reveal to you, indeed. This is a major announcement, I say.”
“What could this possibly be about? Why can’t he just tell us directly, I wonder?”
“Even if he told us directly, he’d probably act like there’s nothing to be scared of.”
“Apparently there is something he fears, though.”
“A woman gone off the deep end, wasn’t it? Not exactly something the two of us could handle.”

The me in the video didn’t bother pausing to consider timing or reply to Father and the others’ conversation. After all, the only audience I’d imagined for this recording was Ren and Itsuki watching it.
“What I have hidden, working in the shadows to reveal to you two the truth of this kingdom… was none other than… the rabbit…”
At that exact moment, I transformed into my Usauni form on screen.

“It is I! Usauni Motoyasu, ribbit! Ren, Itsuki, have you both finally realized just how rotten this kingdom and your companions truly are, ribbit? Thought it was about time to teach you both a lesson, ribbit!”
Bam! I struck a pose. I’d even edited the video crystal to add speed lines for effect.
“Usauni Motoyasu, Shadow Clone Jutsu, I say! Shu-shu-shu-shu!”
With that, the me inside the video crystal showed off an afterimage trick, moving at high speed thanks to my elevated stats.
“To all you Heroes out there, if you found this video crystal even the slightest bit entertaining!”
“Don’t forget to subscribe to the channel!”
“It’d make me super happy if you left a like, ribbit!”

With that, I released the clone technique and, noticing Yuki-chan and the others slightly startled by my transformation, signaled them for an outing. Yuki-chan caught on and shifted into her Filolial form.
“Well then, I’ll be heading out for a while, so farewell, ribbit-byeee!”
“Off we go, then!”
“Departure time!”
“Kuro-chan, keep this a secret from Ren, alright, I say?”
“Got it! Shadow Saint Hero’s awakened and Ren’s gonna play with us, right? I’ll invite Keel later too!”
And with that, the recording stored in the video crystal came to an end. Having watched the footage, Father placed a hand over his face and shook his head as if in despair.
“I mean, there’s no subscribe button or like button on this thing… who on earth taught Motoyasu-kun those video site catchphrases?”
In one smooth motion, Itsuki raised his hand, drew back his bow, and shot the video crystal clean through. It shattered into countless fragments and scattered into nothing.
“I had a feeling this might be the case… don’t you agree, Ren-san?”
“Yeah. If he’d done all that in that form and just kept quiet about it, I would’ve let it slide.”
“And yet here he is, provoking us like this even after we let it go… No matter what, we’re finding him and stringing him up.”
“Agreed.”
And with that, Ren and Itsuki burst out of my house and took off running.
